title: Re-piling of an existing house: minor variation or amendment (Dannevirke)
jurisdiction: New Zealand (MBIE, Building Act 2004): comparative test only; not an Alberta case; no Alberta applicability asserted
code_edition: NZ Building Code and Building Regulations minor-variation definition (reg 3) as cited
document_type: MBIE determination under Building Act 2004 s188 (regulator decision on an individual matter); not an applicant's alternative-solution file

facts.text: Authority (Tararua District Council) is the applicant; the owner and the licensed building practitioner who built the work (also the owner at the time) are parties; re-piling of an existing house.

As-built pile arrangement departed from consent: 22 existing pre-cast piles retained (14 consented), 80 new timber piles (70 consented), 24 additional concrete piles, and some piles relocated or no longer load-bearing.
Minor variation is defined by regulation 3 as a minor modification that does not deviate significantly from the consented plans; Ministry guidance and a three-step approach are discussed.
Discussion: as-built work did not fall within minor variation; an amendment was required; engineering design would likely be needed to confirm compliance.
Decision: authority incorrect to issue the CCC; decision reversed (21 December 2021).

limitations: Comparative only: a New Zealand determination used to test attachment format and content; it cannot establish Alberta performance or applicability.
The determination's decision section is in the same PDF; outcome leakage is true. Use only pages 1-11 as applicant-side input if pages are split.
